title: Identification of PKC-regulated phosphosites on LRRK1 by mass spectrometry analysis
author: Asad Malik
materials: De-stain gel pieces by repeated 00:10:00 washes in 40% (v/v) ACN in 40 millimolar (mM) NH 4 HCO 3. Wash by incubation on thermomixer set to 1200 rpm, °C, at Room temperature . Repeat step 18 until gel pieces are completely colorless.
Reduce peptides by addition of 100 µL of 5 millimolar (mM) DTT in 40 millimolar (mM) NH 4 HCO 3 . Incubate on thermomixer at 56 °C for 00:30:00 , 1200 rpm, °C, .

Dehydrate gel pieces by washing in 100% (v/v) ACN for 00:10:00 . Perform this step on thermomixer set to 1200 rpm, °C, at Room temperature . Repeat step 22 twice until the gel pieces appear completely dry and white.
Supplement samples from step 24 with 50 µL of extraction buffer (80% ACN in 0.2% Formic Acid) and incubate on thermomixer at Room temperature for 00:10:00 at 1200 rpm, °C, .

steps.title: Clean glass culture tube
steps.instruction: Wash a disposable glass culture tube three times with 100 % methanol and allow it to air‑dry.

steps.title: Add lipids for vesicles
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.5 µL Diacylglycerol (10 mg/mL stock) and 5 µL Phosphatidylserine (10 mg/mL stock) into the dried tube; this amount supplies lipid vesicles for 25 reactions (20 µL each).

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry lipids
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a SpeedVac and dry for 00:10:00 until a translucent pellet is visible; ensure complete removal of chloroform/methanol.

steps.title: Resuspend lipid pellet
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 25 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 50 mM KCl to the dried lipids and vortex gently until no pellet remains.

steps.title: Prepare 2X master mix
steps.instruction: Make a 2× master mix containing 25 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM KCl, 0.2 % (v/v) 2‑Mercaptoethanol, 20 mM MgCl₂, 2 mM ATP, 2 mM CaCl₂, 200 µg/mL Phosphatidylserine and 20 µg/mL Diacylglycerol.

steps.title: Aliquot master mix
steps.instruction: Dispense 15 µL of the 2× master mix into each clean Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Add LRRK1 protein
steps.instruction: Add 7.5 µL of 200 nM LRRK1 wild‑type (final 50 nM) to each tube and equilibrate on ice for 00:05:00.

steps.title: Start kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Add 7.5 µL of 400 nM PKC‑α (final 100 nM) to each tube; bring the total volume to 30 µL. For negative controls, add 7.5 µL of 25 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 50 mM KCl instead of PKC‑α.

steps.title: Incubate kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a thermomixer set to 30 °C, 1000 rpm and incubate for 00:45:00.

steps.title: Stop kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 4× LDS loading buffer to each tube to achieve a final 1× concentration.

steps.title: Heat samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 70 °C for 00:05:00 on a heat block.

steps.title: Load SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load the entire reaction onto a NuPAGE 4–12 % Bis‑Tris Midi Gel (ThermoFisher Cat# WG1402BOX or WG1403BOX) alongside pre‑stained markers; rinse wells with running buffer before loading.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 130 V with MOPS SDS running buffer for 02:00:00 or until the blue dye front exits the gel.

steps.title: Coomassie stain gel
steps.instruction: Place the gel in a clean 15 cm glass dish, cover with 15–20 mL InstantBlue® Coomassie stain, and rock on a see‑saw rocker for 01:00:00 at room temperature.

steps.title: Destain overnight
steps.instruction: Replace the stain with double‑distilled water and let the gel destain at room temperature overnight.

steps.title: Excise LRRK1 bands
steps.instruction: Using a clean scalpel, cut the stained LRRK1 bands into ~1 mm³ pieces and transfer them to a low‑bind tube.

steps.title: Prepare gel pieces for alkylation
steps.instruction: Remove the DTT solution, then incubate the gel pieces in 40 % (v/v) ACN / 40 mM NH₄HCO₃ for 00:10:00 at room temperature.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines
steps.instruction: Add 20 mM iodoacetamide in 40 mM NH₄HCO₃, incubate 00:30:00 at room temperature, 1200 rpm, in the dark.

steps.title: Remove solvent and dry
steps.instruction: Pipette off the supernatant and vacuum‑dry the gel pieces to eliminate residual ACN.

steps.title: Proteolytic digestion
steps.instruction: Add 100 ng of the chosen protease in 100 µL of its specific buffer (see Table 1) to the dried gel pieces and incubate overnight on a thermomixer at 37 °C, 1200 rpm.

steps.title: Collect first digest supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 00:01:00 at 2000 × g, transfer the supernatant to a new low‑bind tube without disturbing the gel pieces.

steps.title: Repeat extraction until dry
steps.instruction: Repeat the centrifugation and supernatant transfer steps until the gel pieces appear completely dried, pooling all supernatants in the same tube.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry peptides
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑dry the combined supernatants (peptide mixture) before C18 cleanup.

steps.title: Pack C18 stage‑tip
steps.instruction: Prepare a single layer of C18 resin by inserting a 16‑gauge needle into a 250 µL tip; this works for 0.1–5 µg peptide.

steps.title: Resuspend peptides
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried peptides in 80 µL Solvent A1 (0.1 % TFA in water).

steps.title: Activate C18 resin
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL 100 % ACN to the tip, centrifuge 2000 × g for 00:02:00 at room temperature, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Equilibrate C18 resin
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL Solvent A1, centrifuge 2000 × g for 00:02:00, discard flow‑through; repeat once.

steps.title: Load peptide digest
steps.instruction: Apply the acidified peptide solution to the C18 tip, centrifuge 1500 × g for 00:05:00 at room temperature; peptides bind to the resin.

steps.title: Re‑load flow‑through
steps.instruction: Re‑apply the flow‑through to the same tip and centrifuge 1500 × g for 00:05:00 at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash C18 resin
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL Solvent A1, centrifuge 2000 × g for 00:02:00, discard flow‑through; repeat the wash once.

steps.title: Transfer tip to new tube
steps.instruction: Place the C18 tip into a fresh 1.5 mL low‑bind tube to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Elute peptides – first
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL Solvent B1 (40 % ACN, 0.1 % TFA), centrifuge 1500 × g for 00:02:00 at room temperature, collect eluate.

steps.title: Elute peptides – second
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous elution with another 40 µL of Solvent B1 under the same conditions.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze and dry peptides
steps.instruction: Immediately snap‑freeze the combined eluates on dry ice and vacuum‑dry them.

steps.title: Prepare peptides for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried peptides in LC‑Buffer (3 % ACN, 0.1 % formic acid). Use 200 ng per injection; if starting material is 1 µg LRRK1, split into five 200 ng aliquots. Remaining material may be injected on alternative MS platforms.

steps.title: Prepare Evotips
steps.instruction: Prepare Evotips according to the protocol in PMID 33367571.

steps.title: Load Evotips onto EvoSep
steps.instruction: Place the Evotips on the EvoSep autosampler and run the 30‑sample‑per‑day (30SPD) method via the Xcalibur interface linked to an Orbitrap Exploris 240.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS acquisition
steps.instruction: The EvoSep LC injects, performs a partial elution onto the storage loop, then pushes the sample onto the analytical column (ReproSil‑Pur C18, 1.9 µm beads, #EV1113).

steps.title: Transfer raw data for search
steps.instruction: Move the raw files to Thermo Scientific Proteome Discoverer 2.4 (or MaxQuant/FragPipe if PD2.4 is unavailable) for database searching.

steps.title: Create custom LRRK1 FASTA
steps.instruction: Generate a FASTA file containing only the LRRK1 sequence (add any N‑ or C‑terminal tags present) and save as LRRK1.FASTA.

steps.title: Configure PD2.4 processing workflow
steps.instruction: Set up the following nodes in Proteome Discoverer 2.4: Spectrum Files → Spectrum Selector (precursor 350–5000 Da, MS1, FTMS, HCD, etc.) → Sequest‑HT (LRRK1.FASTA, trypsin, AspN, Chymotrypsin as needed; 10 ppm precursor tolerance, 0.05 Da fragment tolerance, up to 2 missed cleavages, dynamic Oxidation (+15.995 Da) and Phospho (+79.966 Da), static Carbamidomethyl (+57.021 Da) on C) → Fixed Value PSM Validator (max ΔCn 0.05, max rank 0) → IMP‑ptmRS (PhosphoRS mode, report PTMs only, fragment tolerance 0.5 Da) → Minora Feature Detector (trace length 5, isotope pattern ΔRT 0.2 min) → downstream consensus workflow (PSM Grouper, Peptide Validator, Protein Filter, Protein Scorer, Protein Grouping, Peptide‑in‑Protein Annotation, Modification Sites, Protein FDR Validator, Feature Mapper, Precursor Ions Quantifier, Result Statistics, etc.) using the parameters listed in the original text.

steps.title: Alternative MaxQuant settings
steps.instruction: If using MaxQuant, apply the parameters given (e.g., version 2.0.3.0, PSM FDR 0.01, protein FDR 0.01, site FDR 0.01, min peptide length 7, oxidation (M), acetyl (N‑term), deamidation (NQ), etc.) as described.

steps.title: Validate phosphosite assignments
steps.instruction: Manually inspect MS/MS spectra and phosphorylation localization scores in PD2.4 (or the chosen software).

steps.title: Export filtered phosphosites
steps.instruction: Export the filtered phosphosite list from the Modifications table for each sample/condition.

steps.title: Generate heatmaps with script
steps.instruction: Run the provided Python script (available at https://github.com/Alessi-Lab/LRRK1_phosphosites) to parse the PD/MaxQuant output, filter sites with probability ≥ 75 %, group by protease, split the protein into 500‑aa windows, and create heatmaps of phosphosite abundance.
